comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION to my original filing. I first attributed this to a Verified Gate concurrency group that was not keyed per-change, because the first cancellation (04:09:41) coincided to the second with the creation of run 31562353593 for a different change. That was a coincidence, and the hypothesis is refuted by the second occurrence: the mutation job on run 31562494026 ran 04:16:23 -> 04:46:40 and cancelled at 30m17s, matching the first run's 30m16s, with no competing run created at that instant. Two cancellations at the same 30-minute mark is a timeout signature, not a race, and _mutation.yml:34 declares timeout-minutes: 30.

The proven mechanism is instead the all-shards selection. Reproduced locally against change 1615's diff:

    total shards: 7 -> signing, reducer-processors, next-batch, gates, validate, compact-policy, push-policy
    changed: .github/workflows/{_eval-discipline,_optionality,external-integration,structured-output-baseline,test}.yml, tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
    SELECTED: all 7  => all shards selected? True

because .github/workflows/test.yml is listed in global_support and select_shards returns tuple(manifest.shards) whenever ANY changed path matches a global_support pattern.

The title, description, and acceptance criteria have been rewritten accordingly. Leaving the wrong hypothesis recorded here rather than silently deleting it, since the coincidence is a trap the next person may also fall into: distinguish the two by checking whether the durations cluster at the job's timeout-minutes.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INVESTIGATION: premise REFUTED — this is not a concurrency-group collision. Not claiming; reporting back for a scope decision.

## What the evidence actually shows

The cancelled job in run 31560638673 (change 1615 ps2) is a single job, 'mutation (changed behavioral shards on the patchset) / bounded mutation gate'. Its GitHub check-run annotations read:

    The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 30m0s
    The operation was canceled.

Timings: started 03:39:25, completed 04:09:41 = 30m16s. The identical pattern appears on run 31560592163 (change 1620 ps2): 03:38:14 -> 04:08:29 = 30m15s, same two annotations.

The 04:09:41 coincidence with run 31562353593 (change 1624 ps2) being created is exactly that — a coincidence. 04:09:41 is 30m00s after the job started; the job died on its own clock, not because another change's run pre-empted it.

## Why the concurrency-group theory does not hold

1. .github/workflows/_mutation.yml pins 'timeout-minutes: 30' on the 'bounded mutation gate' job. That is the documented cause GitHub annotated.
2. Only ONE job was cancelled in each run; all 14 others completed. A workflow-level concurrency cancel terminates every in-flight job in the run, not one.
3. The concurrency group is ALREADY keyed per change: gerrit-verify-GERRIT_CHANGE_ID with a run_id fallback. GERRIT_CHANGE_ID is a required workflow_dispatch input, so it resolves; distinct changes get distinct groups.
4. The cross-change cancellations I could actually attribute were all same-change supersedes, which is intended: 1615/1 superseded by 1615/2, 1620/1 by 1620/2, and 1618/2 (03:56, run 31561628712) by 1618/2 (03:59, run 31561809295, which then succeeded).

So AC1 and AC2 are already satisfied by the current key, and AC3 cannot be reproduced because the behaviour it describes does not occur.

## The real defect

The bounded mutation gate does not fit inside its own 30-minute budget on a Gerrit patchset. When it blows the timeout, the job conclusion is 'cancelled'; gerrit-verify.yaml's vote job aggregates run conclusions (mutation is in its needs list) and casts Verified -1 with a 'CANCELLED:' message that carries no test signal. A recheck just spends another 30 minutes and hits the same wall, which is the starvation the ticket describes — the symptom is real, the mechanism is not.

Only AC4 survives intact and is worth keeping: a cancellation/timeout is not a test verdict and should not read as a bare Verified -1.

## Options (needs a decision — each changes CI behaviour beyond this ticket's stated scope)

a) Raise or remove timeout-minutes: 30 on the mutation job.
b) Tighten the gate so a shard finishes inside the budget (shard the selection further / bound mutants per shard).
c) Distinguish timeout from failure in the vote step so a timed-out run does not present as an unexplained CANCELLED -1 (this is AC4).

(b)+(c) look like the right pair, but that is a materially different change from 're-key the concurrency group', so I stopped rather than implement it under this ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
STOP BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: the corrected defect is ALREADY FIXED on current origin/main. Recommending we do NOT apply the planned change.

## The two timeouts ran against a workflow that no longer exists

Both timed-out runs used main at the time of dispatch, not the patchset, for the reusable workflow:

| Run | main at dispatch | mutation jobs | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31560638673 | 57d19254 | 1 job, no matrix suffix | cancelled at 30m16s |
| 31562494026 | 2c0fec01 | 1 job, no matrix suffix | cancelled at 30m17s |

57d19254 is 'ci: establish mutation gate walking skeleton' — a SINGLE 'bounded mutation gate' job that ran every selected shard serially under one timeout-minutes: 30. That is why all-shards blew the budget, and it is the shape the ticket's proof describes.

Commit ac0f62be11 'Complete phased mutation gate core' landed on main at 2026-08-12 03:35 UTC and replaced it with a selector job plus a per-shard parallel matrix: 'matrix: {shard: selected_shards}', so each shard is now its own job with its OWN 30-minute budget.

## The all-shards case now passes

Run 31563668309 (main at ac0f62be) selected ALL 7 shards. Every one succeeded:

| shard | duration |
|---|---|
| push-policy | 0m39s |
| compact-policy | 0m41s |
| validate | 6m04s |
| next-batch | 7m25s |
| signing | 13m09s |
| gates | 11m25s |
| reducer-processors | 20m22s |

Worst shard 20m22s against a 30m budget — about 32% headroom. This is precisely AC4's reproduction scenario (a change touching a global_support path selecting all 7) and it completes cleanly, so AC1 is already satisfied.

## Why I did not apply the planned fix

1. Dropping .github/workflows/test.yml from global_support would REDUCE gate coverage to solve a problem that no longer exists. The over-broad selection is real but it is no longer harmful now that shards run in parallel — it costs runner slots, not a red vote.
2. Raising timeout-minutes is unnecessary: no shard job on the new workflow has come close to 30m. Raising it now would be tuning against a number measured on the retired serial workflow.
3. The self-blocking concern in AC5 dissolves with it: a change touching mutation-shards.toml selects all 7 shards, and all 7 now pass.

## What is actually blocking change 1615

1615's runs were dispatched while main was still at the walking-skeleton commit. It needs a REBASE onto current origin/main (de267b06, which contains ac0f62be) so its Verified run picks up the parallel matrix — the standard 'pre-analysis failure -> rebase, never recheck' path. No repository change is needed for it.

## Residual work worth keeping

AC3 stands on its own merit and is independent of all the above: a timed-out or cancelled mutation job still aggregates into a bare 'CANCELLED:' Verified -1 that carries no test signal. That is defence-in-depth against the next timeout, whatever causes it, and is the only part of this ticket I would still implement.

Separately, the 'select mutation shards' STEP failed outright on runs 31563192064 and 31563305610 (both on ac0f62be). I could not read the logs — the runs were still in progress — so I am flagging it as unverified rather than diagnosing it. If it reproduces it deserves its own ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Filer's note, owning the error: BOTH of my hypotheses on this ticket are refuted, and the investigator's two comments above have it right.

1. First filing - Verified Gate concurrency group not keyed per-change. Refuted by me: the second cancellation hit the same 30-minute mark with no competing run created at that instant.
2. Corrected filing - one global_support path selects ALL shards and busts timeout-minutes: 30. The SELECTION half is real and reproducible (change 1615 touches .github/workflows/test.yml, so select_shards returns all 7 shards), but it is NOT a defect: ac0f62be had already replaced the serial walking-skeleton gate with a per-shard parallel matrix giving each shard its own budget, and a real all-shards run passed with a worst shard of 20m22s. My two timeouts came from runs dispatched while main still carried the OLD serial workflow - reusable workflows resolve at main's ref, not at the patchset - so they were a rollout-window artifact that a rebase clears.

The trap in both cases was inferring a mechanism from run metadata without checking which version of the reusable workflow the run actually executed. The durable lesson for the next person: when a reusable-workflow job fails oddly, first read the 'Uses: ...@refs/heads/main (<sha>)' line in the job log and confirm that sha is the workflow you think you are debugging.

Change 1615 is unblocked and rebased onto current origin/main (which also now carries 06335f71b1 'Skip mutation gate for pre-gate patchsets'); its patch set 3 already has LLM-Review +1. I am leaving the disposition of this ticket to the investigator and the coordinator - I am only correcting the misleading title I authored.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
TRIAGE RECORD + a correction to my own earlier reading.

Re-scoped this ticket to the one defect that survives investigation: the Verified -1 message carries no triage signal. The two refuted premises are preserved in the comments above — (1) the concurrency group is not keyed per change (refuted: the group already keys on GERRIT_CHANGE_ID, and only ONE job was cancelled per run where a concurrency cancel would kill all of them), and (2) all-shards selection exceeds timeout-minutes 30 (refuted: fixed on main by ac0f62be's per-shard parallel matrix — run 31563668309 selected all 7 shards and all 7 passed, worst 20m22s of a 30m budget).

## Correction

I earlier reported the 'select mutation shards' step failing with 'fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/changes/25/1625/1'. That was a misread: those log lines were cyan-highlighted ECHO of the step's own script source — the checkout action's embedded default error string — not its output. The actual failure is

    mutation_gate.py: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'select' (choose from run, smoke)

This is version skew, not a live defect. The reusable workflow resolves at main's ref and calls the new 'select' subcommand, while those runs execute scripts/mutation_gate.py from a patchset checkout based BEFORE ac0f62be added it. A rebase fixes it; 1625 is being rebased. No new ticket.

## Why this strengthens the remaining defect

It is a second, completely different cause producing the same uninformative vote. Compare what Gerrit showed for each:

| runs | actual cause | Gerrit message |
|---|---|---|
| 31560638673, 31562494026 | mutation job hit timeout-minutes: 30 | CANCELLED: <url> |
| 31563192064, 31563305610 | selector step: invalid choice 'select' (version skew) | CANCELLED: <url> |

A timeout on a healthy patchset and a stale-base version skew are indistinguishable from the vote. The first needs no author action, the second needs a rebase — and the message tells an agent neither. That is precisely what the re-scoped work fixes.

## Design constraint found while scoping

lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action hardcodes its message as "${STATUS}: <run url>" and exposes no input for custom text. I verified this at the pinned SHA a1c036a5 (v1.1.2) and on the action's current main, and v1.1.2 is the latest tag — so there is no upstream bump available. The detail must therefore be posted as an additional comment-only review rather than by enriching the vote message in place. Vote semantics are untouched.

## Conflict check vs change 1627

1627 ('Skip mutation gate for pre-gate patchsets', status NEW) touches .github/workflows/_mutation.yml and tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py. My change touches gerrit-verify.yaml, a new scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py, and a new tests/scripts/ test. No file overlap; I will not touch either of 1627's files.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — pushed as Gerrit change 1633 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1633), commit ac8eb91a, branched from origin/main at 06335f71b (which already contains 1627, so no collision with the mutation session).

## What landed in the change

- scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py (new): pure summarize() rendering each non-successful job as TIMED OUT / CANCELLED / FAILED with its duration and html_url. Returns '' when everything succeeded, so a green run posts nothing.
- .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml: two new steps in the vote job plus a key-cleanup step; 'checks: read' added; the trusted sparse-checkout now fetches the summarizer alongside the normalizer.
- tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py (new, 22 tests), tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py (new, 11 tests).
- tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion_port_heldout.py: one assertion updated, see below.

## AC4 refined during implementation — please note the deviation

AC4 as written expected a step using the action's 'comment-only: true' input. I did NOT use it. The action hardcodes MESSAGE="${STATUS}: <run url>", and comment-only merely suppresses the labels — it posts the SAME canned text, so it cannot carry any detail. The comment is therefore posted with a direct 'ssh ... gerrit review <change>,<ps> --message ...' call carrying no --label, which is a comment-only review in Gerrit's own terms. The substance of AC4 (detail posted, no label cast) holds; the mechanism differs. Asserted by test_the_comment_step_casts_no_label, which greps the step for --label / Verified= / Code-Review=.

## Observability-only, enforced by tests rather than asserted in prose

- the cast step still reads vote-type: ${{ steps.normalize.outputs.vote-type }} (unchanged)
- vote.needs is unchanged and pinned by a test
- exactly one gerrit-review-action invocation exists in the vote job
- both new steps are continue-on-error and run AFTER the cast, so if they break the vote is already on the change and the run cannot redden
- the new steps are guarded on vote-type != 'success'

## Security note

The summary reaches a remote 'gerrit review --message' over ssh inside single quotes, and job names are patchset-influenced (matrix shard names come from mutation-shards.toml). The summarizer strips ' and \\ and every control character except newline; three tests cover it, including a hostile shard name that tries to close the quote and append a command. The summarizer is fetched from the default branch via the existing trusted sparse-checkout, so the vote job still never executes patchset code.

## Pre-existing test I had to touch

tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion_port_heldout.py::test_workflow_sparse_checkout_fetches_only_the_py asserted the literal line 'sparse-checkout: scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.py'. The sparse-checkout is now a two-entry block, so I rewrote that assertion to parse the YAML and check the invariant it actually cared about: the normalizer is still named, every pattern is a .py file, and cone-mode is still false. Intent preserved, literal-string coupling removed.

## Local gates

835 passed, 1 skipped across tests/scripts/ + the workflow tests; scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py OK; make lint (ruff + zizmor + actionlint) and make typecheck both clean.

Waiting on LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PROGRESS — plan-review certified, ps2 green, ps3 in flight.

## Attestation now certified

rebar review-plan --status: {ok: true, verdict: certified, currency_basis: file_impact, verified_at_sha 990d102a}. It took four rounds and the failures are worth recording, because none of them found a defect in the implementation:

1. STALE HEAD. The first PASS signed against origin/main while I rebased mid-review, so it was stale on arrival. Do not move the worktree HEAD while review-plan is running.
2. PLAN LAGGED CODE (AC4). The reviewer blocked on the plan naming gerrit-review-action's 'comment-only: true' as the delivery mechanism, correctly reasoning it cannot carry text — comment-only is a LABEL switch, not a message switch, so it re-posts the same canned '<STATUS>: <url>'. The code had used a dedicated SSH 'gerrit review --message' step since the first patchset; only the description was stale. It also cited ADR-0023 (CI account is SSH-key-only, no HTTP password), which independently rules out a REST path.
3. PLAN UNDER-SPECIFIED (mechanics). Blocked on not saying how annotations reach summarize(), and on a raw ssh defaulting to port 22 (closed on the Gerrit host) without key/known_hosts installation. Again the implementation already did all of it. Rather than assert it in prose I made each detail verifiable — six new workflow-parsing tests now pin port 29418, the chmod 600 key + known_hosts install, the ^[1-9][0-9]*$ change/patchset guard, the if: always() key removal, and both API fetches — and added AC9/AC10 to match.
4. DESCRIPTION TOO LONG. 8001 chars against an 8000 admission cap, self-inflicted by fixing (2) and (3) with more prose. Rewrote rather than shaved one character: 8001 -> 6247, keeping every load-bearing specific and cutting redundancy. Detail belongs in code and tests; the plan carries only what a reviewer needs to judge feasibility.

Lesson for the next agent: the gate reviews the PLAN, never your diff. Update the description the moment the design changes — recording a deviation in a comment (as I did) does not reach the reviewer.

## Gerrit

- ps2: LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1 (CI run 31575196657 SUCCESS). The earlier Verified -1 was a real failure in my own change, not a known-flake: the comment-hygiene guard rejected a raw GitHub run id in a test docstring, which failed the lint job AND all four pytest cells from one root cause. Fixed by replacing the id with durable prose. No recheck would have helped.
- The earlier LLM-Review -1 was bugfix-size-attestation: 268 non-test lines over the 150-line bugfix floor with no attestation on this ticket. Cleared by the signed PASS above.
- ps3 pushed (rebased onto 990d102a) and awaiting votes. I did NOT submit the green ps2: it predates the six tests that enforce AC9/AC10, so landing it would have closed this ticket against acceptance criteria nothing verified.

Local gates at the ps3 tree: 17/17 workflow tests, full targeted suite green, check_verify_gate_parity.py OK, check_comment_hygiene.py clean, make lint (ruff + zizmor + actionlint) and make typecheck clean.

compiled_state.description:
A cancelled or timed-out job in the Gerrit Verified Gate casts `Verified -1` with a message
that is exactly `CANCELLED: <run URL>`. It names no job and gives no reason, so triage means
opening the run and reading job conclusions by hand.

OBSERVABILITY ONLY: when the gate votes +1/-1 must not change, only what the -1 carries.

## Why the message is empty

`gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `vote` job casts with `lfreleng-actions/gerrit-review-action`, which
self-builds `MESSAGE="${STATUS}: ${SERVER_URL}/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${RUN_ID}"` and has
no input for custom text (checked at pin a1c036a5 = v1.1.2 and on the action's current main;
v1.1.2 is its latest tag). Its `comment-only: true` input does NOT help — it only suppresses
labels and still posts that same self-built text. It is a label switch, not a message switch,
so the detail cannot be delivered through that action at all.

Two real causes produced the identical `CANCELLED: <url>`: the `bounded mutation gate` hitting
`timeout-minutes: 30`, and `select mutation shards` failing with `invalid choice: 'select'` on
a stale base. Only the second needs author action (a rebase), and the vote cannot tell them
apart.

## Approach

1. `scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py` (new, trusted): pure `summarize()` maps a list-jobs
   payload plus check-run annotations to one line per non-successful job — job name, TIMED OUT
   vs cancelled vs failed, duration, `html_url`. Returns "" when all jobs succeeded.

2. A `Summarize the jobs that did not succeed` step in `vote`, guarded on the normalized
   vote-type not being `success`, gathering both inputs with `GITHUB_TOKEN`:
   - jobs: `gh api --paginate repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/jobs`,
     collected via `jq -s -c '{jobs: .}'`, passed as `JOBS_JSON`;
   - annotations: for each failure/cancelled/timed_out job,
     `gh api repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` (a job id IS its
     check-run id), assembled into a `{"<job id>": [...]}` map passed as `ANNOTATIONS_JSON`;
     best-effort, a failed read degrades wording but must not fail the step.
   This is why the workflow needs `checks: read`: GitHub reports a timed-out job as
   `conclusion: cancelled` and says "exceeded the maximum execution time" ONLY in the
   annotation, so without it a timeout is indistinguishable from a supersede.

3. A `Post the triage detail to Gerrit` step posting via a dedicated SSH
   `gerrit review <change>,<patchset> --message '<text>'` — the call the action makes
   internally — with NO `--label`, so it comments rather than votes. A raw `ssh` must
   reproduce what the action does internally: port `29418` (the default 22 is closed on the
   Gerrit host); `secrets.GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY` written with `chmod 600` and
   `vars.GERRIT_KNOWN_HOSTS` written to `~/.ssh/known_hosts` with
   `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, as `vars.GERRIT_SSH_USER`@`vars.GERRIT_SERVER`; change and
   patchset rejected unless they match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, mirroring the action's own guard; the
   key removed in an `if: always()` step. REST is unavailable — per ADR-0023 the CI account is
   SSH-key-only with no HTTP password.

Both new steps run AFTER the cast and are `continue-on-error`, so the vote is already on the
change before they execute and a fault cannot redden a passing run.

The script is sparse-checked-out from the default branch like
`scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.py`, so patchset code never runs in the vote job. Because the
summary is interpolated into a single-quoted remote argument and matrix job names derive from
`.github/mutation-shards.toml` (patchset-controlled), `summarize()` strips `'`, `\` and all
control characters except newline.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` (summarize + SSH comment + key-cleanup steps;
  sparse-checkout list; `checks: read`)
- `scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py` (new)
- `tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py` (new)
- `tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py` (new)
- `tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion_port_heldout.py` (sparse-checkout assertion
  becomes structural now that the step fetches two scripts)

Does NOT touch `_mutation.yml` or `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` — change 1627 owns those.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: a job whose annotation says it exceeded its maximum execution time renders as timed
      out, naming the job and its duration; unit test asserts the text.
- [ ] AC2: timed out, cancelled-without-annotation, and failed render with different wording;
      unit tests cover all three.
- [ ] AC3: an all-successful payload returns "", so a `+1` run posts no comment; unit test.
- [ ] AC4: the summary is posted by an SSH `gerrit review --message` step passing no `--label`
      (casting neither Verified nor Code-Review), guarded on vote-type != `success`; a test
      parses the workflow and fails if `--label`, `Verified=` or `Code-Review=` appears there.
- [ ] AC5: the cast step's `vote-type` still reads `steps.normalize.outputs.vote-type`, and
      `normalize` is unchanged; asserted by a test.
- [ ] AC6: `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` still passes — `vote.needs` unchanged.
- [ ] AC7: both new steps are `continue-on-error` and ordered after the cast; asserted by
      tests, so a fault in the comment path leaves the vote already cast.
- [ ] AC8: a job name containing a single quote cannot escape the remote command's quoting;
      unit test feeds a hostile shard name through `summarize()`.
- [ ] AC9: the SSH step uses port 29418, installs the key with `chmod 600` plus `known_hosts`,
      validates change/patchset against `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, and removes the key in an
      `if: always()` step; asserted by tests parsing the workflow.
- [ ] AC10: the summarize step fetches this run's jobs from `actions/runs/<id>/jobs` and
      per-job annotations from `check-runs/<id>/annotations`, passing them as `JOBS_JSON` /
      `ANNOTATIONS_JSON`; asserted by tests parsing the workflow.

## Verification

    python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py -q
    python -m pytest tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py -q
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py
    make lint && make typecheck

file_impact.reason: vote job gains the summarize + comment-only steps, checks: read, and the summarizer in the trusted sparse-checkout
new trusted script rendering non-successful jobs as TIMED OUT / CANCELLED / FAILED
new unit tests for the summarizer, including ssh-quoting sanitization
new tests pinning the observability-only boundary (vote semantics unchanged)
sparse-checkout assertion rewritten structurally now that the step fetches two scripts
